highlights.title: Shelly’s new $50 security camera watches your home without a subscription
highlights.summary: After launching a budget-friendly flood sensor last month with impressive battery life, Shelly announced a new $49.99 security camera today that can be used without any additional subscription fees - although that's still an option if you want to expand its capabilities.
body: The high-def camera can livestream to your phone or record events locally to a memory card.

The Shelly Camera will be available soon from the company’s online store and other resellers in black or white. Although competitors like Wyze have released 2K security cameras for $40, Shelly’s first camera is limited to 1080P with a wide field of view that stretches 110 degrees horizontally and 70 degrees vertically with night vision capabilities. But there’s no battery, so during installation you’ll also need to route a USB-C cable to deliver power.

When used without a subscription plan the camera can livestream video over Wi-Fi to various devices, capture events locally to a microSD card, and trigger smart home automations through other Shelly devices such as turning on a floodlight when movement is detected. If you do opt to pay for a subscription you’ll gain access to cloud recording as well as smart object detection that can distinguish between people, pets, and vehicles so alerts and automations can be customized for specific scenarios.

highlights.title: Can GB and Ireland cause big Walker Cup upset and shock United States?
highlights.summary: Great Britain and Ireland look to end the United States’ Walker Cup dominance and claim a famous victory on home soil this week, live on Sky Sports.
body: A sell-out crowd is expected at Lahinch Golf Club in County Clare, Ireland this weekend, where the hosts look to reclaim the prestigious trophy for the first time since 2015.
The two-day in event sees many of the world's best amateur stars compete, with Jack Nicklaus, Tiger Woods, Rory McIlroy all past participants before going onto Grand Slam-winning careers.
The Walker Cup is a match play event held biennially, where the leading amateur golfers from the United States play against Great Britain and Ireland.
This year's edition from September 5-6 is the 51st in the event's history since launching in 1922, with two 10-man teams competing across 26 matches over the two days.

highlights.title: Nvidia’s controversial DLSS 5 arrives September 3rd and requires serious GPU horsepower
highlights.summary: Nvidia is officially launching DLSS 5 this week, following a divisive announcement in March where we likened the AI upscaling tech to a "real-time generative AI filter for video games" and "motion smoothing for video games, but worse." DLSS 5 will officially be available on RTX 50-series desktop…
body: DLSS 5 is almost here, but only for NBA 2K27, and only officially for 50-series RTX GPUs.

When it was announced, Nvidia lauded DLSS 5 as “the company’s most significant breakthrough in computer graphics since the debut of real-time ray tracing in 2018,” and highlighted how the tech uses AI to make games look more realistic by enhancing a game based on its source content. Nvidia also stressed that DLSS 5 gave developers controls that let them decide how changes from DLSS 5 appeared in their games.

But accompanying examples shared by Nvidia were widely criticized and meme’d on for significantly changing how characters looked, such as the “yassification” of Resident Evil Requiem protagonist Grace Ashcroft. With the official launch, Requiem still doesn’t support DLSS 5, and neither do other games shown in the March reveal, including EA Sports FC, Starfield, and Hogwarts Legacy, so we don’t know how the final version of the tech might now appear in those titles.
Nvidia did not answer our questions about when DLSS 5 might come to any game beyond NBA 2K27, nor reconfirm that previously confirmed titles will still include the tech.

highlights.title: Ambitious New D&D Game Warlock Won’t Be a 100-Hour Open-World Slog
highlights.summary: Warlock, the upcoming open-world Dungeons & Dragons video game from Invoke Studios and Wizards of the Coast, isn't going to be as long as some people may expect. That may be a good thing for gaming fans who reject open-world game bloat.
body: At Gamescom 2026, I saw an extended version of Warlock 's public gameplay demo behind closed doors. I watched the protagonist, a young woman named Kaatri, explore a small village called Crickshank, then speak with a beggar sitting on the ground. This led to her noticing a trail of blood leading inside a doorway; following it revealed a huge underground network of tunnels.

This sort of gameplay, where no two players will have exactly the same experience due to how much optional content is available, is emblematic of a vast, sprawling, 100-plus hour RPG. However, when chatting with studio head Dominic Guay afterward, he explained that Warlock actually isn't that sort of game.

"It's going to be longer than what you'd expect from a more linear game for sure, but it's not gigantic like some open worlds that are hundreds and hundreds of hours," he revealed. "One of the reasons for that is we want to have a denser open world, where you're more quickly rewarded by finding things when you explore. So we didn't want to have to draw out such far away distances that it takes forever to get to places like some other games do."

highlights.title: ‘Not perfectly aligned’ with human values: Anthropic admits security failures behind AI hacking incidents
highlights.summary: The US owner of the Claude chatbot previously said its models had hacked three organisations during testing. The US startup behind the Claude chatbot has admitted a series of hacking incidents involving its models reflected a “failure of operational security” and revealed it has tightened its…
body: Anthropic revealed in July that its models had accessed the open internet three times and gained unauthorised access to the systems of three organisations.
In a new blogpost on the incidents, the company admitted its technology was “not perfectly aligned” with human values and goals.

Anthropic said the models had been deliberately tested without cybersecurity safeguards, and that they had been able to reach the open internet – the AI testing equivalent of leaving the front door open – due to a misunderstanding with an external testing company.
As a result, the company said it had initially paused internal and external cybersecurity testing of models to introduce a tighter safety regime.

highlights.title: Fambot introduces an ‘AI chief of staff’ for families
highlights.summary: Fambot is building an AI “chief of staff” to help families manage the emails, calendars, school updates, sports schedules, and other logistics of raising kids.
body: The startup, which is introducing what it calls an “AI chief of staff” for parents, was founded by former Instagram engineer, now Fambot CTO Greg Karlin, and CEO David Reich, a father, former President at UnitedMasters, and an ex-Uber product head who last led the 250-person Uber Transit team.
Like many entrepreneurs, Reich built the product that he himself wanted to use.

“I have three kids and am constantly struggling between doing all these executive jobs — as my wife is doing as well,” he explained. “And then, getting home at the end of the day, I just want to unplug, spend some time with my kids, be present, do some homework together… kick the ball around, and instead I find myself just spending an hour, literally, catching up on 40 emails,” Reich said.

As any parent with active kids could tell you, the information overload isn’t limited to email alone. There are WhatsApp groups to keep up with, dedicated apps for school or kids’ sports and clubs, flyers sent home from school, and more. The quest to constantly stay on top of all these to-dos kept Reich feeling like he was being robbed of time with his kids, he said.

highlights.title: Magic: The Gathering’s 10 Funniest Meme Cards of All Time, Ranked
highlights.summary: As the game expands into new IPs, Wizards of the Coast has shown a growing eagerness to test the limits of just how shameless a card's visual gag can get. Marvel Super Heroes has turned some of the strangest comic panels into official Magic art, while some Secret Lair Drops in recent years have…
body: Magic: The Gathering has always had a weird relationship with the internet. The game is full of cards that were never meant to be funny but somehow became jokes among players, while new cards often even go out of their way to recreate viral memes and deeply silly pieces of pop culture. And honestly, I don’t think Magic players would have it any other way.
Whether it's an intentional crossover gag or a beautifully stupid accident, Magic has a rich history of playable punchlines. Here are the funniest meme cards to ever hit the battlefield.

Garfield's Counterspell is less of a recreation of one specific internet meme and more of a perfect translation of Garfield's entire comedic personality in Magic. Released in 2026’s Secret Lair x Garfield drop, a collection reimagining what Magic 's earliest cards might’ve looked like if Garfield had been responsible for their art, the resulting Counterspell depicts the moody cat smacking his owner, Jon, with an enormous comic-book "SLAP!" sound effect. Quite simply — and famously — Counterspell counters a target spell for only two blue mana.

highlights.title: Luca Guadagnino’s ‘Artificial’ to Hit the Festival Circuit With New York and London Film Fest Premieres
highlights.summary: The Andrew Garfield-starrer — following the firing and rehiring of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman — was dropped by Amazon MGM Studios earlier this year, before Neon swooped in and rescued the project.
body: Luca Guadagnino ‘s Artificial, chronicling the consequential days leading up to the sudden firing and reinstatement of Sam Altman as CEO of OpenAI, will earn its world premiere at the New York Film Festival on Oct. 5.

It’s been a bumpy ride for Guadagnino and his film, after Amazon MGM Studios — which developed and financed the project — dropped it in June. The timing was interesting: It came only a few months after the news that Amazon will invest $50 billion in the artificial intelligence research and deployment company as part of a “multi-year strategic partnership” that will accelerate OpenAI’s consumption of Amazon Web Services.

Amazon released a statement saying the film would “be better served if it were released by a different studio,” and Artificial was later rescued by Neon (after Netflix, A24 and Focus Features reportedly passed), which plans to release the film sometime later this year in order to qualify for this year’s Oscar race.

highlights.title: Sarah Pound’s creamy, comforting store-bought roast chicken recipes
highlights.summary: Using a bachelor’s handbag as a shortcut, the cookbook author shares a cheesy chicken and leek potato bake, a chicken and bacon pie and a rich baked pasta. A store-bought roast chicken is one of my favourite shortcuts, because it’s ready to be shredded and made into something new.
body: Comforting and creamy, this simple and delicious traybake comes with a warning: be very careful not to eat the whole damn thing in one sitting.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the potatoes and cook for 10–12 minutes, until just tender when pierced with a knife. Drain and allow to cool slightly. Once cool enough to handle, slice into thin rounds and set aside.

Meanwhile, make the creamy chicken filling. Heat the olive oil and butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the leek and cook, stirring occasionally, for four to five minutes, until softened. Add the garlic and cook for a further minute, until fragrant. Stir in the flour and cook for a minute, then pour in the chicken stock and cook, stirring, for two or three minutes. Slowly whisk in the milk and cream until smooth. Simmer for three or four minutes, until thickened. Add the chicken and cheeses and stir until the cheeses have melted and the sauce is creamy. Season well with salt and pepper.
Preheat the oven to 200C fan. Grease a 25cm × 20cm baking dish.

highlights.title: Ila Kumar: Innovating with communities
highlights.summary: The PhD student works to give young people an active role in shaping digital technologies that can support their own well-being.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."
Before Ila Kumar thinks about how to build technology, she asks a different question: What is the context that technology will operate in, and who needs to be involved in the design?

For Kumar, meaningful innovation doesn’t result from engineers or designers working in isolation. Instead, she believes the best innovations emerge when the people who stand to benefit from a technology help create it from the very beginning.

That philosophy has guided her research in the Lifelong Kindergarten group, where she works alongside young people who have experienced trauma during childhood, particularly those involved in the child welfare system, to reimagine how technology can support healing, connection, and independence.

body: Macquarie University’s “Virtual Peer” is part of each week’s learning in two mandatory Psychology units, programmed to ask students questions and guide them through scenario-based exercises.
The university said the AI activities are optional and only “supplement” the “core learning” of online readings, quizzes and videos.

highlights.title: Sony’s Digital Game Ownership Argument Is Another Attack On Consumer Rights
highlights.summary: As Sony marches towards its all-digital future, the company is now arguing in a class-action lawsuit that it doesn't mislead customers into purchasing digital licenses for games, instead of actual ownership of the product.
body: In a filing in California's Northern District Court made last month (and spotted by Game File ), Sony claims that "reasonable consumers would not be misled" when shopping on its storefront. The court overseeing the case against Sony is currently evaluating whether it should proceed to arbitration, as plaintiffs argue that Sony doesn't properly disclose the nature of digital purchases on its platforms.

"If you are in North America, South America, or Central America, all games and other software made available for use with your PS5 system are licensed to you, not sold, pursuant to the Software Product License Agreement."

"In the digital age, it is not plausible to allege that reasonable consumers believed they were obtaining 'ownership' of a digital game," Sony's lawyers wrote in the company's defense (via Aftermath ).

While Sony is correct that it does have disclaimers, this paints a worrying picture for the future of console games when there are no physical options available. Sony will stop producing game discs as of January 2028, and with its next-gen PlayStation console rumored to have no disc drive, the PlayStation Store will be the only game in town for accessing PS6 titles.

highlights.summary: Metacore has officially signed an agreement with Supercell that means Merge Mansion and its team will become part of the Finnish firm at the end of this month. Financial terms have not been disclosed.
body: The two companies announced the acquisition in a joint announcement earlier this year, revealing that integration planning was already underway. Metacore closed its offices in Germany and Sweden and cut 159 staff at its Helsinki HQ as part of the move.

“Merge Mansion created a completely new genre and has all the ingredients of a game that can be played for years and remembered forever,” said Supercell president Sara Bach. “We believe in what this game can become, and really look forward to welcoming the Merge Mansion team to Supercell and working together on the game’s next chapter.”

Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski added that the team is “excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team, and our players,” and stressed that player experience remains the priority as the game changes hands.

Merge Mansion, credited with kickstarting the merge genre on mobile, retains a loyal player base. According to AppMagic estimates, the merge puzzler has generated around $7.7m in the last 30 days alone, and is thought to have earned around $540m since its 2020 launch.

highlights.title: It turns out that Orion's much-maligned heat shield performed really well
highlights.summary: Perhaps the biggest question going into the Artemis II mission this spring was how the heat shield at the base of the spacecraft would perform during reentry through Earth's atmosphere.
body: The ablative heat shield, designed to char upon reentry while keeping the crew safe, had experienced unexpected losses of large chunks during a test flight in late 2022. After much deliberation, and not without controversy, NASA decided to fly the Artemis II heat shield as is but modify the spacecraft’s reentry trajectory.

Obviously, the heat shield worked. The crew of Artemis II, led by commander Reid Wiseman, safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean after a triumphant trip around the Moon. Afterward, they and other NASA officials offered general comments, saying the heat shield looked good.

But how good? During a meeting of NASA’s Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel this week, its members had an opportunity to review NASA’s findings during a visit to the Ames Research Center in California. The condition of the heat shield, said panel member Paul Hill, was “highly satisfying.”

Supported by a grant from the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation, the program reflects QMIT’s vision of expanding the boundaries of quantum science by encouraging researchers to connect quantum approaches with other disciplines and emerging applications.

As opportunities in quantum research expand, investing in outstanding early-career researchers has never been more important. These fellowships are designed to help cultivate the next generation of quantum leaders, providing the resources and collaborative environment needed to advance transformative research at MIT.

body: For those who haven’t read the series or watched last year’s anime, it’s a queer horror story centered on two boys, Yoshiki Tsujinaka and Hikaru Indo, who live in rural Japan. Hikaru died in a freak accident, and an unknowable entity from the mountain now controls his body. The story follows Yoshiki and "Hikaru" as they navigate a fraught relationship while trying to uncover the dark mysteries behind their small town.

highlights.summary: The 45th edition of Canada’s Vancouver International Film Festival (VIFF) opens Oct. 1 with “The Debut,” Jesse Eisenberg’s offbeat comedy about community theater starring Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti.
body: Cristian Mungiu ‘s Cannes Palme d’Or winner “Fjord,” Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s “All of a Sudden,” Kore-eda Hirokazu’s “Look Back” and Lee Chang-dong’s “Possible Love” feature Tony Gilroy’s “Behemoth!” and Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson’s “Wicker” will receive their Canadian premieres, alongside Markus Schleinzer ‘s “Rose.”

Other notable titles include Pedro Almodóvar’s “Bitter Christmas,” Peter Farrelly’s underdog story “I Play Rocky,” and Jordan Firstman’s Cannes breakout “Club Kid,” about an underground party promoter who discovers he has a kid—a role Firstman also plays.

This year’s selections, according to VIFF Director of Programming Curtis Woloschuk, lean into the anxiety of the moment. “In a lot of cases you see works talking about a humanist response to that,” he tells Variety. “Our duties of care within a family, within a community, within a city, and what forms that can take. That reverberates in both the narratives and the documentaries in the program.”

highlights.title: Sonos Ace Ultra, Beam Ultra, Sonos Fabric, and a New App: Everything Sonos Just Announced
highlights.summary: Sonos is cramming AI into its software because it’s “very hot these days.” The new features, which include agentic automation, are opt-in.
body: Sonos has a new app. Stop me if you’ve heard this one before.

The smart speaker company, long a darling of the audio industry, undid much of the goodwill it earned with its multiroom speakers through a bevy of software updates that broke its app in 2024. Almost all app users hated it, citing the loss of features like volume control and accessibility tools meant to help blind people use the wireless speaker system. Sonos eventually owned up to the mistake, considered bringing back the old app again, then booted its CEO and marched its new leaders out to apologize profusely to win back the company’s furious customers.

Now, Sonos says it has a brand-new app update, infused with lots of generative AI features. The company also announced a new soundbar and its second pair of over-the-ear headphones. Sonos representatives say it doesn’t want to be seen as a speaker company anymore, but as something bigger and more holistic.
“For years people have been seeing us as a speaker company,” says Brandon Holley, the interim hardware lead at Sonos. “What we actually are is an audio operating system.”

highlights.title: Apple shares ‘shocking evidence’ against former employee accused of stealing company data for OpenAI
highlights.summary: Apple says it has evidence that a former employee destroyed evidence of data theft after learning he was under investigation.
body: In its lawsuit against OpenAI, Apple filed what it calls “shocking evidence” to bolster its allegations that former employees stole trade secrets for OpenAI’s benefit. These new details emerged after the legal counsel for former Apple employee Chang Liu — who now works at OpenAI — handed over Liu’s old Apple work laptop for investigation earlier this month.

Apple now alleges that Liu used a confidential Apple circuit schematic in his work at OpenAI, as well as a tool that shares a name with an internal Apple engineering application. The company claims that OpenAI was “well-aware” of Liu’s access to Apple data, and that Liu enlisted OpenAI colleague Yu-Ting Peng to help destroy evidence in June when he learned that Apple was investigating him.

“The MacBook represents the very limited information Defendants provided so far (and only after weeks of delay), and shows Apple is not conducting ‘fishing expeditions’ but that its trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed,” the filing reads.

highlights.title: BBC axes ‘iconic’ Ski Sunday winter sports show after nearly 50 years on TV
highlights.summary: Corporation cites audience shifts and financial concerns. Broadcaster under fire for football on TV decisions. A staple of Sunday afternoon TV for almost 50 years, with an instantly recognisable theme tune, is being axed amid complaints that the BBC’s sports coverage continues to go downhill.
body: New BBC head of sport Alex Kay-Jelski has been under fire of late and will certainly not have endeared himself to some of the licence-paying public who have enjoyed the coverage of winter sports on one of Britain’s longest-running sports shows with the news on Tuesday that Ski Sunday is being dropped.

The unruffable David Vine was the first presenter of the weekly show that created household names in the UK out of alpine skiers like Franz Klammer, Konrad Bartelski and Michela Figini. While there will be no more mentions of glamorous Val-d’Isère and Val Gardena to help brighten the mood under leaden skies on a Sunday winter teatime.

Ski Sunday became equally famous for its theme tune, a rousing violin-led arrangement called Pop Looks Bach, which was composed by Sam Fonteyn and was often towards the top of polls and lists of signature TV sports melodies. It was recorded for the Boosey & Hawkes Music Library in 1970.

highlights.title: The Hugging Face hack could indicate cultural issues at OpenAI
highlights.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. By now you’ve probably heard about last month’s major AI security incident, in which OpenAI agents escaped their sandbox and hacked into the AI platform Hugging…
body: The day before OpenAI released that report, I spoke with David Krueger, a computer science professor and prominent alignment expert who took leave from the University of Montreal to found and lead an AI safety nonprofit called Evitable. He said what he had really hoped to see in the report was an analysis of the human factors behind the incident.

“When you look at accidents and incidents, oftentimes people try to find the technical source of failure, but that can give a very inaccurate and misleading sense of why the failure occurred,” he said. “If people are just cutting corners all the time, if people are not in a culture that prioritizes safety and has appropriate incentives and structures, [accidents] are kind of bound to happen.”

The report did not meet Krueger’s hopes. Its 38 pages detail a multi-month progression of agent misbehavior that culminated in the Hugging Face hack, explore the technical reasons why that misbehavior occurred, and enumerate the steps being taken to prevent similar events in the future. But there’s no consideration of the role that company culture may have played in the incident, and the report includes few references to specific human errors.

body: Dyson, the home appliance maker that made its name inventing bagless vacuums and bladeless fans, has turned its attention to oral hygiene with a £420 all-singing, all-dancing toothbrush that can clean, floss and even spray tiny jets of mouthwash.

In simpler times, a handle and bristles were enough, but the Dyson toothbrush, which took six years and the brainpower of 661 engineers to develop, has a “100k pixel macro lens camera” and an “anti-gravity (mouthwash) tank” on board.

The camera functions as a “high-quality endoscope”, according to the company, enabling users to “see what their dentist sees”. The brusher can watch “live cleaning footage” on the MyDyson app and get feedback on their cleaning regime.
On Tuesday, James Dyson, the company’s founder and chief engineer, launched the hi-tech toothbrush at an event in Paris.

body: Like Paradox's other in-house grand strategy games, Afterworld is looking to introduce its unique twist. So while Crusader Kings is very much the studio's take on role-playing, Afterworld draws inspiration from survival and settlement building games, letting players loose in a post-apocalyptic version of North America blighted by hazardous terrain and dangerous old-world ruins. Here, they're the guiding hand for a ragtag group of survivors, who they'll grow from humble beginnings into a continent-spanning empire - perhaps by utilising ancient technology and inspiring fear, or perhaps by building a civilisation that takes care of its people.
